premise.headline: Hallway sleuths and hostage manners collide.

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Hall Pass Noir
jokes.joke: I tried working as a private detective, but my first case was in a school hallway, which is impossible. You can’t shadow anyone there. Every six seconds a locker explodes, a kid stops dead, and a teacher goes, “Sir, why are you crouching behind the water fountain?” I said, “Surveillance.” She said, “That’s a sixth grader with a hall pass.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Elementary, My Dear Bladder
jokes.joke: I used to think I was a master detective. I could read a room, clock every detail, notice things nobody else caught. Then I became a substitute teacher. I spent forty minutes convinced the kid in the back was plotting something — intense eye contact, nervous energy, kept shifting in his seat. Turns out he just really needed to use the bathroom. I had cracked the case of the wiggling third-grader.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: People-Pleasing Hostage
jokes.joke: I'm such a people-pleaser that if I ever end up being captured, I'm going to be a ridiculously hospitable hostage. I’ll be zip-tied to a radiator in a damp basement, my kidnapper will hand me a glass of tap water, and I’ll be like, 'Oh, you didn't need to use a coaster, it's just concrete! And honestly, the ropes are perfectly snug. I love what you've done with the murder room, by the way—is this real exposed brick?'

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Private Eye Blunder
jokes.joke: I decided to try my hand as a private detective. Trench coat, shady alley meetings, the works. Last week I'm tailing a hot lead through the neighborhood when suddenly I'm being captured—hands tied, bag over my head. Turns out it was my wife who spotted me lurking and thought I was a creep. She dragged me inside and made me explain why I was following her from the grocery store. Private detective? More like publicly divorced.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Hallway Hero
jokes.joke: I tried being a private detective once, but the only case I ever solved was why the school hallway smelled like fear and cafeteria tater tots. I strutted around like a noir hero until a teacher stopped me and said, “Sir, you don’t even work here.” Hard to look mysterious when you’re being escorted out past the lost‑and‑found box.

scores.comment: Clear comic misread with good wording, but it uses a classroom/bathroom situation rather than the school hallway concept, so prompt fit drops.
Strongest premise in the batch, with vivid escalation and a clean people-pleaser hostage angle; a bit long but lands well.
Understandable and in form, but the capture setup feels forced and the final line is more wordplay than a strong comic turn.
Clean first-person setup using exactly two concepts, but the payoff is familiar and mild rather than sharply surprising.

Clean escalation, the locker-exploding chaos earns the setup, and the final exchange lands with good timing. 'That’s a sixth grader with a hall pass' is a satisfying snap. Slightly familiar fish-out-of-water shape but executed with real rhythm.

Genuinely fresh angle—the people-pleaser hostage is a non-obvious conceptual turn and the brick detail earns a real laugh. 'Murder room' is the best single phrase in the batch. Runs slightly long but earns the space. Strong human-level joke.

'Publicly divorced' is a tidy button but the turn is telegraphed early—once the wife appears you know where it's going. Competent construction, familiar shape. The punchline redeems a predictable middle but doesn't fully surprise.

Tater tots and fear is a mild smile, not a laugh. The escorted-out line is a restatement of the premise rather than a turn. Lost-and-found is a nice concrete detail but the joke ends before it builds to anything. Competent filler.
Strong staging and concrete imagery; the dialogue grounds the absurdity and delivers a solid, relatable punchline.
Competent stand-up rhythm, but relies on a predictable premise and misses the specific hallway constraint in favor of a general classroom setting.
Decent narrative misdirection, but the escalation feels cartoonish and the bit closes on a weak, strained pun.
Features strong, evocative imagery like cafeteria tater tots, though the final turn is a bit expected compared to the setup.
Solid school chaos visuals, mild teacher payoff.
Clever misread twist but safe substitute-teacher trope.
Strong escalation and vivid hostage politeness.
Generic school intrusion bit with weak mystery angle.
Solid premise with clear first‑person voice; the hallway chaos image works, though the ending lands more as a continuation than a sharp turn.
Clean and coherent, but the turn is predictable and the payoff mild; competent but not especially memorable.
Strong angle with a clear escalation and a crisp final image; the hostage‑hospitality contrast lands well.
Fun premise and a decent twist, though the final line leans on a familiar joke shape; still a real, workable bit.
